narrative.t: Between 24 Jun 2026 and 22 Oct 2026 (NISAR, 8 passes, track 151 descending), the open water in the box (sea or a large lake running past the box edge) stayed about the same: 332 km² on 24 Jun and 333 km² on 22 Oct.
narrative.s: Water-dark = smoothed brightness below 58 of 255 (valley after the darkest peak in the 24 Jun histogram); main body = largest connected dark patch, 334 km² at its widest

narrative.t: On the map, 0.00 km² that was water-dark on 24 Jun no longer is by 22 Oct (orange, "water lost": drying shore), and 0.05 km² became water-dark (blue, "water gained").
narrative.s: NASA GIBS · NISAR GCOV display tiles, 24 Jun vs 22 Oct 2026; same water threshold, first vs last pass, only within 300 m of the dark water bodies

narrative.t: Across the whole box, 0.32 km² became much darker in radar (new water, wetter or smoother ground) and 0.00 km² became much brighter (rougher or bare ground, structures, debris or crops).
narrative.s: NASA GIBS · NISAR GCOV display tiles, 24 Jun vs 22 Oct 2026; more than 4 robust σ (12 of 255 levels) after 5×5 smoothing; 0.10 km² on steep, shadowed terrain left out

narrative.t: The largest single patch (marker 1) is 0.05 km² of water gained, around 31.376° N, 35.479° E (brightness 59 → 55 of 255).
2.7 km² jumped by more than 4× its own normal pass-to-pass wobble, most of it (1.7 km²) between 16 Sep and 10 Oct; the same test on the first pair flags 0.07 km², a rough false-alarm level.
narrative.s: Per-pixel temporal anomaly over 8 passes (median absolute successive difference)

narrative.t: The plant signal (HV-like green channel) fell by 13% across the box, consistent with harvest, drying or clearing.
Grouping pixels that behave alike over time gives 6 zones; none changes strongly as a whole, and the "dark all season" zone (likely open water) covers 309 km².
narrative.s: Unsupervised k-means on per-pixel time profiles; labels are interpretations

narrative.t: NASA EONET lists no natural events; USGS lists no M4+ earthquakes within about 50 km of this box in this period. That is context, not proof of cause.
narrative.s: NASA EONET v3 and USGS FDSN event APIs, box ± 0.5°
